data.body:
INVESTIGATED under rebar-debug. Verdict: NOT a defect — intended-behavior / authoring convention. rebar does not inject these line breaks anywhere.

MECHANISM (proven, not assumed)
A Gerrit "change description" for these changes IS the git commit message, and Gerrit serves it byte-for-byte.
- `ChangeInfo.description` is None on change 982 (and on every recent change sampled), so the separately-editable description field is unused repo-wide. The text being viewed is the commit message.
- The message Gerrit serves for change 982 (`GET /a/changes/982/revisions/current/commit`) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to `git log -1 --format=%B 992b0656d`. Gerrit adds and transforms nothing.
- That commit's body was authored hard-wrapped: max line length 79 over 37 body lines. The newlines are in the git object itself.

DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE AGAINST A CODE INJECTOR (this is the decisive test)
Measured max body line length over the 20 most recent commits on gerrit/main. The result is BIMODAL and author-dependent:
  hard-wrapped : 992b0656d=79, 93df22461=79, 87478f047=79, 23e51a014=78, 3e2747816=77, f0cf30a0e=75, 2e2fe3f7d=75, 1e7e5c946=74, 2281280d2=72
  unwrapped    : b3953a0da=286, 9808b1217=207, 55f2b8036=200, 5f9f22673=194, be8a0c059=179, dcc90ced4=167, f3dbe32b0=146, bc838aed2=129
A code path that injected breaks would produce UNIFORM widths. It does not. The variation tracks who wrote the commit.

INJECTION-SITE HUNT CAME BACK EMPTY (searched, negative result stated explicitly)
- `grep -rn "textwrap|TextWrapper|wrap_width|line_width|\.fill(" --include='*.py' src/rebar/` (excluding tests) -> ZERO matches. No wrapping primitive exists anywhere in the package.
- `grep -rniE "SetCommitMessage|/edit/message|changes/.*/message|revisions/.*/description|set-description" --include='*.py' src/rebar/` -> ZERO matches. rebar has no code path that can write a Gerrit commit message or change description; review_bot/gerrit_client.py's only write is POST /revisions/{rev}/review.
- No prompt asset under src/rebar/llm/reviewers/, src/rebar/llm/prompting/, .rebar/prompts/ or src/rebar/_guides/ instructs fixed-width/columnar output.
- The one rebar-generated Gerrit text (the review-bot comment) DE-wraps rather than wraps: review_bot/adapter.py:122 does `.replace("\n", " ")[:240]`. Real posted bot messages are <=63 chars.
- Re-confirmed bug 4e21's Jira fix cannot reach this path: `text_to_adf` lives in _engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/ and nothing under review_bot/ imports it.

AUTHORITY
The hard-wrapping is what the Gerrit server itself asks for: pushing change 982 produced `remote: commit fbb7f66: warning: too many message lines longer than 72 characters; manually wrap lines` (Gerrit's bundled commit-message-length validator, not configured by rebar). Plus git's own ~72-column body convention.

HONEST GAP FOUND (the actually useful outcome)
rebar documents NO commit-body wrapping convention: searching CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, docs/*.md and src/rebar/_guides/*.md for "72 col|hard-wrap|wrap the body|column width|fixed column" returns nothing, and there is no commit-message linter in CI (verify-commit-ticket checks only the trailer). That silence is why commit styles are split between the two modes above and why this reasonably looked like a bug. Recommended follow-up is DOCUMENTARY, not a code fix: state the ~72-column body convention in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Closing as not_a_bug per the rebar-debug not-a-bug guard: a mechanism is not a defect, and no authoritative source is violated by the current behaviour.
